q: Does the open-pan-genome behavior and the ~60,000-gene estimate still hold when the analysis is extended to the ~10x larger set of Bacillus cereus s.l. genomes now available in NCBI/BV-BRC (2024-2026 deposits, ~5000+ genomes), and does the accumulation curve finally show any hint of saturation at this scale?
basis: This replication used 27 genomes and reproduced the open-pan-genome trend, but Bazinet's original scale was 114-498 genomes (2017 deposits). Public genome counts have grown ~10x since. Testing whether openness persists at 5000+ genomes is the natural sanity check on C1/C6 and would firm up the pan-genome-size estimate.
next_steps: Pull the current BV-BRC B. cereus s.l. genome set (filter species membership by 95% ANI to Ames/ATCC 14579), subsample at N = 100, 500, 1000, 2500, 5000, run Roary or Panaroo at 80% identity on each, fit a Heap's-law model to the pan/core accumulation curves, and report the alpha exponent (alpha < 1 = open). Free tier: NCBI Datasets + Panaroo on uicgpu.

q: How much of the exact 251-vs-2415-vs-600 core-gene-count discrepancy is due to Roary's strict CD-HIT/BLAST clustering vs Bazinet's HaMStR profile-based ortholog recovery, as opposed to genuine sampling effects?
basis: The replication's core count varied 10x (251 to 2415) depending on genome subset and blastp identity, while Bazinet reported ~600 on his 114-genome set with HaMStR. A head-to-head Roary vs Panaroo vs OrthoFinder comparison on the same input would isolate the method contribution from the sampling contribution.
next_steps: On the same 27-genome input already annotated with Prokka, run Panaroo (with paralog-splitting and gene-model correction), OrthoFinder, and PIRATE side-by-side. Report core-gene counts at identical thresholds (99% presence, 80% identity). Predict: Panaroo will lift the core well above Roary's 251 on the divergent 26-genome set.

q: Do specific virulence and antimicrobial-resistance (AMR) gene families (cry, ces, hbl, nhe, cytK for B. thuringiensis/B. cereus toxins; pXO1/pXO2 markers for B. anthracis; bla, tet, van for AMR) distribute across the pan-genome in the ecologically-structured pattern predicted by Bazinet's clade model, or do they cross clade boundaries by horizontal gene transfer?
basis: Bazinet's paper deliberately downplayed the accessory content; the paper's phenotype-linked pan-GWAS (Scoary) was not reproduced here. Whether virulence/AMR genes are clade-restricted or HGT-mobile is a first-order biological question that follows directly from the pan-genome table but was not exercised.
next_steps: Take the Roary presence/absence Rtab (Run A, 27 genomes) already in evidence/, annotate the 48118 gene clusters against CARD (for AMR) and VFDB (for virulence), and compute per-cluster clade-specificity using Fisher's exact test against the Clade-1/2/3 assignment. Flag genes with clade-specificity p > 0.5 as HGT candidates. All free-tier tools.

q: How does the B. cereus s.l. pan-genome compare to those of the closely-related outgroup Bacillus subtilis group and the more distant Bacillus megaterium group -- does the openness/size scale with clade breadth, or is B. cereus s.l. anomalously open?
basis: Bazinet analyzed one species-complex in isolation. Comparative context (is 60k genes normal for a Bacillus complex, or unusually large?) requires running the same pipeline on peer Bacillus complexes. This was not done.
next_steps: Assemble matched 100-genome sets for (i) B. cereus s.l., (ii) B. subtilis group, (iii) B. megaterium group; run identical Prokka + Roary(80% i) pipeline on each; report pan-genome size, core size, and Heap's-alpha per group. Predict: cereus s.l. openness (alpha) is comparable to subtilis but shifted upward in raw pan size due to the extra ~1.5 Mbp of accessory content characteristic of the group.

q: Can a supervised ML classifier trained on the accessory-gene presence/absence matrix reliably distinguish B. anthracis from its near-neighbors in B. cereus s.s., given that anthracis is nested inside cereus s.s. at >99.98% ANI and can only be told apart by pXO1/pXO2 plasmid content?
basis: This replication confirmed the anthracis-nested-in-cereus result (C4) but did not test whether the confounding is severe enough to break automated species-ID from the chromosomal accessory genome alone. This matters for BV-BRC's own species-assignment pipeline and for biosurveillance.
next_steps: Use the panacc_clade1_new.Rtab presence/absence matrix as features, anthracis/non-anthracis as label; train a leave-one-strain-out logistic-regression and random-forest classifier; report per-strain confusion, top-k discriminating gene clusters, and whether removing all pXO1/pXO2-linked gene clusters collapses accuracy to chance. Scikit-learn only; runs on uicgpu CPU in minutes.
